subject: Post-call: PayPioneer pilot affordability & batching options
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Vega <daniel.vega@paypioneer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + pilot affordability options

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the 30-minute walkthrough this morning. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed next step so we can move to a concrete pilot that fits your budget constraints.

Key pain points you called out
- High per-call cost for customer-facing GPT moments (authorization & dispute flow) — current internal estimate: ~$0.006/token at peak.
- Latency spikes during peak hours causing a conversion hit on mobile flows.
- Security/audit requirements: logs must be retained 90 days and keys managed in your KMS.

Goals you shared
- Proof-of-value pilot against authorization flow with clear TCO and latency tradeoffs.
- Target effective cost that doesn’t increase monthly run-rate meaningfully — rough target you mentioned: keep incremental spend under $25k for the pilot window.
- Minimum acceptable P95 latency: sub-250ms for interactive flows.

Redwood proposed framing (high level)
- Pilot scope: 6-week pilot, staged on hosted Redwood API with option to transition to Dedicated if performance/commitment warrants.
- Two cost tracks to present:
  1) Conservative (lower engineering effort): hosted, standard model (quantized), aggressive batching and prefix caching — expected effective token cost ~ $0.0018–$0.0024 (assumptions below).
  2) Performance-first (dedicated pool): slightly higher committed minimum, lower tail latency, effective token cost ~ $0.0014–$0.0019 after batching + cache.

Assumptions used for quick math (will send a workbook):
- Average prompt+response per request: 400 tokens
- Observed cacheable prefix ratio for your auth flow: 28% (we can push higher with light template hints)
- Average batching factor we can achieve for async paths: 12–18 tokens per batch depending on burstiness

What I’ll send you today
- Draft SOW + pilot statement of work (attached)
- Cost workbook with per-configuration line items and break-even analysis (attached)
- Call recording stub for internal reference (attached)

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm that a 6-week hosted pilot with a total pilot budget of up to $27k would be feasible on your side? If not, tell me the hard cap.
2) If yes, please confirm the decision owner for pilot approval (PO/Finance contact).
3) We propose a short technical kickoff next Tue (Jul 27) — what time window works for your engineering lead?

If you want, I can also sketch a very small-lift option that targets a $15k cap by narrowing sample size and leaning on aggressive cache-friendly templates.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: paypioneer-sow-draft.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: paypioneer-cost-calculation.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: call-recording-20270722.mp3 (audio/mpeg)]
From: Daniel Vega <daniel.vega@paypioneer.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: payments-ops@paypioneer.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 12:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pilot affordability options

Irene — thanks for the quick write-up. This is helpful. A few things from our side:

- Budget: the hard cap for a pilot that I can get signed without a heavier procurement cycle is $25k total. Preferably all-in (Redwood fees + infra).
- Latency: we need P95 under 350ms end-to-end (our instrumentation has some network overhead); 250ms would be ideal but 350ms is the absolute ceiling for this pilot.
- Security: we will need the audit log export for any requests touching PHI/account numbers. KMS integration is mandatory.

If you can show a configuration at or below $25k with a clear hypothesis on 1) expected token burn, 2) expected cache hit with minimal changes to our templates, and 3) worst-case latency numbers, we can proceed.

For the lower-cost option: we are open to a more aggressive quantized model if you can quantify the quality delta. Can you include a short A/B quality guardrail we can run on 2–3 critical prompts?

Availability: Fri afternoon PT or Mon morning PT for a short follow-up.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Vega
CTO, PayPioneer
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Vega <daniel.vega@paypioneer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pilot affordability options

Thanks Daniel — good constraints to anchor on. See two concrete pilot options below; I attached the detailed workbook with line-item math. Short summary: both options target being at-or-below your $25k cap by narrowing sample size and applying caching/batching levers.

Option A — Lean hosted PV (aim: stay <= $25k)
- Scope: 4-week focused pilot (reduced from 6) on Redwood hosted API, end-to-end on your auth flow sample (20k requests simulated / week).
- Cost anchors: model base + infra = $0.0032/token nominal
- Levers applied: prefix caching (28% hit), batching factor ~14 average on async queue, light quantization for response path (minimal quality impact in our evals).
- Expected effective cost: ~ $0.0019/token -> estimated total pilot spend $22k (includes 10% buffer for burst).
- Latency: expected P95 ~ 280–320ms observed in similar pilots; we’ll instrument traces and add a canary route with stricter SLO.
- Deliverables: quality A/B on 3 prompts, latency dashboard, runbook for moving to Dedicated.

Option B — Committed minimal Dedicated (if you prefer guaranteed tail behavior)
- Scope: 6-week pilot on a small dedicated pool with reserved capacity & burst option.
- Cost anchors: committed infra + slightly lower per-token engine cost = $0.0025/token nominal
- Levers applied: same caching + batching assumptions; expected effective cost ~ $0.0015/token with similar cache/batch numbers.
- Estimated total pilot spend: $34k (above your stated cap) — but we can present a blended commercial (one-time pilot credit) to bring net to $25k for the pilot window if a PO/commit to transition is signed.

Attachments: the workbook includes a sensitivity table so you can move cache hit / batch factor sliders and see the total spend. I’ve also included a 3-prompt A/B evaluation we can run during the first week.

Next steps (proposed)
1) If Option A looks viable, confirm the $25k cap and decision owner and we’ll issue a shortened SOW today.
2) If you prefer Option B, confirm whether PayPioneer can consider a short term PO to offset the pilot (we can propose a refundable credit against the first month of Dedicated).
3) Schedule a 20-minute follow-up to align on exact prompt set and instrumentation (Fri 4pm PT or Mon 9am PT suggested).

Can you confirm availability for Fri 16:00 PT?

Best,
Irene

[Attachment: paypioneer-cost-calculation.xlsx]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 18:37:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: PayPioneer pilot pricing flex

Irene — quick internal note so we’re aligned before we push the shortened SOW.
- Marketing OK to allow a 10% pilot discount (bring Option B from $34k -> $30.6k). If Daniel confirms a PO that transitions to Dedicated within 90 days we can apply an additional $5.6k credit to hit the $25k net.
- Karthik: can ops enable prefix hints and tweak the cache TTL so we can realistically push cache hit closer to 40% on week 1? If yes, that materially improves the effective cost (shifts Option A to ~ $1.6–$1.7 per token effective in best case).
- We should include a clause limiting pilot-exposed data footprint and confirming KMS setup — procurement will need that.

Irene — I’ll greenlight the 10% discount on the SOW and you can send the shortened version to Daniel. Keep me looped.

—Marissa
